title: Parent-child relationship links enable cross-record linking
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links into the account directory. These explicit relationship identifiers allow records of students and parents/guardians to be linked together within the directory, increasing the ability to correlate data across individuals and contexts.

title: Directory can combine data of different individuals via stored family links
description: Once stored in the account directory, account records and parent-child links enable combining data of different individuals in one place. This supports linkage between a child account and related parent accounts, potentially revealing household or family associations.

title: Written account records likely contain direct or unique identifiers
description: Writing account records to the directory likely involves unique account references or other identifiers needed to maintain directory entries and relationship links. Such data makes the involved individuals directly identifiable or readily identifiable within the system.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not enumerate exact fields, so this is inferred from the need to maintain account records and relationship links.

title: Stored directory records can serve as attributable evidence about relationships
description: Persisted account records and parent-child links in the directory can later be used as evidence that a specific person was associated with a given child or account. This may reduce deniability regarding family relationships or account associations.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the stored records are treated as authoritative evidence; the description does not state evidentiary use explicitly.

title: Propagation of grading-held relationship data into the account directory may exceed necessity
description: The grading service propagates account records and parent-child relationship links into a separate account directory. If the directory does not strictly need all relationship details for its function, this creates unnecessary disclosure by making the data accessible in another repository.
uncertainty_note: The necessity of storing parent-child links in the account directory is not fully specified, so the excessiveness depends on intended directory functionality.

title: Directory storage exposes relationship data to a predetermined additional party set
description: By writing the records into the account directory, the grading service makes personal data available to the systems, administrators, and processes with access to that datastore. This broadens exposure to a predetermined set of parties beyond the grading service itself.
uncertainty_note: This assumes the datastore is accessible by multiple authorized components or operators, which is typical but not explicitly stated.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that family relationship data is stored in the directory
description: Students and parents may not be aware that the grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links into the account directory, especially if the directory is a backend store not directly visible to them.
uncertainty_note: User notice and transparency mechanisms are not described, so this is a plausible but not certain threat.

title: Limited ability to rectify or erase incorrect relationship links in the directory
description: If parent-child relationship links are stored in the account directory, data subjects may lack a direct mechanism to correct or remove inaccurate or outdated links. This creates a risk of insufficient intervenability over stored relationship data.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not mention any rectification or erasure controls; threat is based on their possible absence.

title: Potential data minimization violation from storing relationship links in the directory
description: If the account directory does not strictly require parent-child relationship links or full account record details for its purpose, writing this data there may process more personal data than necessary, creating a GDPR data minimization compliance risk.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the directory genuinely needs these relationship attributes for its defined purpose, which is not fully specified.

title: Potential insufficient support for rectification or erasure of directory relationship data
description: Storing account and parent-child relationship data in the directory creates compliance risk if data subjects cannot effectively access, correct, or erase inaccurate or obsolete entries. This threatens support for data subject rights.
uncertainty_note: The existence of data subject rights handling is not described; this is a risk inferred from the storage of relationship data.

title: Full backup contains stable identifiers enabling cross-context linkage
description: The nightly backup ships full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud hosting provider. Account-directory fields and record keys are likely to include stable unique identifiers (such as student/staff IDs, usernames, email addresses, or internal account IDs), allowing the provider or anyone with access there to link records about the same person across datasets and over time.
assumptions: Assumes the full backup includes account-directory identifiers or record keys that remain stable across backups.

title: Backup transfers identified student and staff data to the hosting provider
description: Because the flow sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party cloud hosting provider, the transferred dataset likely contains directly identified personal data rather than anonymized records. This makes data subjects directly identifiable within the backup at the receiving environment.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory and grade records include direct identifiers such as names, usernames, email addresses, or institutional IDs.

title: Grade and assignment records can serve as attributable evidence about individuals
description: Full grade records and assignment data can be attributed to specific students and possibly instructors, creating evidence of performance, submissions, and academic interactions that may later be used to prevent those individuals from denying associated claims or events.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with identifiable students and possibly staff through the included account directory or embedded identifiers.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly mention signatures, audit logs, or metadata fields; this threat is grounded in attributable content of the records themselves.

title: Presence of individuals in the education system can be detected from replicated backups
description: Once full backups are replicated to the cloud hosting provider, the provider can observe recurring communications and stored backup contents that reveal whether particular students, staff, grades, or assignments exist in the system and when they change. This enables detection of a person's participation or activity in the service.
assumptions: Assumes the provider can access backup contents or meaningful metadata about included records and backup timing.
uncertainty_note: Detection here is inferred from the provider's visibility into recurring backup transfers and replicated data, not from an explicitly described monitoring feature.

title: Propagation of full academic records to a third-party provider may exceed necessity
description: The flow propagates full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external cloud hosting provider. Sending the complete dataset to a third party for backup/replication may disclose more personal data to another service than is strictly necessary, especially if only a subset, encrypted form, or minimized backup would suffice.
assumptions: Assumes the provider is a separate party and that full-content replication is not strictly required in this exact form to achieve backup/hosting objectives.

title: Full nightly backup may process an excessive amount of personal data
description: The described flow ships full grade records, assignments, and the entire account directory every night. This suggests bulk transfer of all available academic and account data, which may exceed the amount of personal data functionally needed for backup or replication if incremental, selective, or minimized approaches could be used instead.
assumptions: Assumes a full backup is not strictly necessary every night and that less data-intensive alternatives may exist.
uncertainty_note: Necessity depends on operational design; the excessiveness judgment is therefore somewhat context-dependent.

title: Nightly replication may occur more frequently than functionally necessary
description: The flow performs nightly shipment of full records to the cloud hosting provider. If backup or disaster-recovery objectives could be met with less frequent or incremental transfers, this creates unnecessary repeated disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes nightly full replication is more frequent than required for the service's recovery objectives.
uncertainty_note: The description does not provide recovery-point objectives, so frequency excess cannot be stated with full confidence.

title: Personal academic data is shared with an additional predetermined external party
description: The backup makes full academic and account data accessible to the cloud hosting provider, a fixed external party known at design time. This increases exposure of sensitive student and staff data beyond the primary assignment and grading service environment.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud hosting provider is organizationally separate from the service operator and can access the replicated data in some form.

title: Students and staff may be unaware that full records are replicated to a third-party host
description: Data subjects whose grades, assignments, and directory information are included in the nightly backup may not be aware that their full academic records are being transferred to and stored with a third-party cloud hosting provider for backup and replication purposes.
assumptions: Assumes this third-party backup/replication practice is not clearly communicated to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Awareness depends on notices and institutional transparency, which are not described.

title: Data subjects may lack practical ability to erase or rectify replicated backup copies
description: When full records are replicated nightly to a third-party hosting provider, correcting or deleting personal data may become harder because backup copies can persist outside the primary service. This can limit data subjects' ability to have inaccurate data rectified everywhere or to have data removed when no longer relevant.
assumptions: Assumes backup copies are retained and not immediately synchronized with rectification/erasure actions across all replicas.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify retention or deletion mechanisms for backups.

title: Full third-party backup may violate data minimization expectations
description: Sending full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud hosting provider every night may process more personal data than necessary for the stated backup/hosting purpose, creating a risk of violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes less intrusive backup designs could satisfy the same operational need.
uncertainty_note: Whether this is truly noncompliant depends on the actual necessity analysis and safeguards, which are not provided.

title: Third-party replication of sensitive academic records may lack a clearly justified lawful basis
description: Replicating full grade records, assignments, and account-directory data to an external cloud hosting provider introduces additional processing by a third party. If this transfer and hosting arrangement is not properly justified under the applicable lawful basis and governance arrangements, it creates a lawfulness noncompliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy law requires a documented lawful basis and appropriate processor/controller arrangements for this external processing.
uncertainty_note: The flow description alone cannot confirm absence of a lawful basis or contractual controls; this is a compliance risk indicator rather than proof of violation.

title: Backup replication can undermine fulfillment of data subject rights
description: Because full personal records are copied to a third-party hosting provider, the system may struggle to fully support access, rectification, and erasure rights across all replicated copies unless dedicated controls exist. This creates a risk of insufficient support for data subject rights.
assumptions: Assumes backup copies are retained separately and rights-handling processes do not automatically propagate to all replicas.
uncertainty_note: This depends on operational controls not described in the flow.

title: Grade records are linkable through unique student identifiers
description: The grade records database likely stores records keyed by unique student identifiers or equivalent local identifiers so the grading service can assemble student, parent, and teacher views. This enables linking multiple grade entries and related records to the same student across assignments and time.
uncertainty_note: The presence of a unique identifier is strongly implied by the need to build per-student views, but the exact identifier type is not specified.

title: Grade records likely contain identified student information
description: To build views for students, parents, and teachers, the grading service likely reads grade records that include directly identified student information or records readily tied to named individuals. This creates an identifying-information threat at the source data store.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not explicitly list fields such as names, but identified or readily identifiable records are a reasonable assumption for grade reporting.

title: Grade records can serve as attributable evidence about a student's performance
description: Stored grade records can be attributed to a specific student and used as evidence of academic performance, making it difficult for the data subject to deny the associated claims once the service reads and presents them.
uncertainty_note: This is based on the records being tied to individual students; whether this is problematic depends on governance and context.

title: Read access may expose grade data to dynamically determined viewers
description: The grading service reads grade records in order to build views for students, parents, and teachers. Because the service is the component that determines which viewer receives which view, there is a risk that personal grade data becomes accessible to a dynamic set of parties broader than functionally necessary if access scoping is not strict.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on how the service authorizes viewers; the description only establishes that multiple audience types are served from the same underlying records.

title: Students may be unaware that their grade records are repurposed into multiple audience views
description: The grading service reads grade records to construct separate views for students, parents, and teachers. Data subjects may not be fully aware that the same underlying records are processed and disclosed in different contextual views for multiple recipient categories.
uncertainty_note: This is plausible from the multi-audience use described, but the presence or absence of notices or transparency mechanisms is not provided.

title: Building multiple views from full grade records may violate data minimization
description: If the grading service reads more grade-record content than each specific audience view requires, the processing could exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose, creating a data minimization compliance risk.
uncertainty_note: This is a conditional compliance threat: the description does not specify whether the service fetches only necessary fields or entire records.
